clips.linkedin:
Give AI your key pages and the question each should answer, and it rewrites the openings that miss.

Ranking on Google no longer predicts who gets quoted in AI answers. One analysis put the overlap between top organic links and AI-cited sources at under 20%, down from around 70% in early 2024.

A model wants a passage it can lift cleanly and a claim it can stand behind. So the first job is your opening paragraphs. AI reads the first 200 words of each page, tells you whether the question gets answered, and drafts a new opening where it doesn't.

The second is the vague claims. It lists every superlative, suggests a checkable version and flags where you don't have a source yet. Deciding what's true stays with your team.

The podcast voices are AI-generated. The prompts, episode and article are at https://manual-focus.co.uk/blog/the-citation-moved-off-the-page/
clips.text: Get AI on this. First job, get AI on your opening paragraphs. Give it the URLs of your most important pages and the question each one is meant to answer. It reads the first two hundred words of each, tells you whether that question actually gets answered, and drafts a new opening wherever it doesn't. Second. Get your AI to hunt down the vague claims. Same pages. It lists every superlative and fuzzy claim, suggests a specific, checkable version of each, and flags the ones where you don't have a source yet. Deciding what's true and finding the evidence stays with your team.
